+title: Find why the first streamed chunk did not reach the consumer in cancellingAStreamingAnswerFinishesTheStreamWithCancellationError
+---
+## What
+
+Found during ^cx1type. One plain `swift test --skip-build` run (right after a parallel stress run ended, load average about 16 over 5 minutes) had one issue:
+
+- `AnswerCancellationEntryPointTests.cancellingAStreamingAnswerFinishesTheStreamWithCancellationError`, display name "cancel() finishes a streamEvents answer with CancellationError, leaving the consumer what it already received": `BoundedWait.swift:114:25: Issue recorded` from `BoundedWait.conditionReached("the first streamed chunk at the consumer")`.
+
+So the consumer did not get `HookedSessionBackend.firstStreamedChunk` inside the bound, before the test called `session.cancel()`. The wait was added in ^zr22hpd (commit ce3c0bf). The next 3 full runs passed (1487 + 17 + 19).
+
+The ^cx1type change (`isWorkCancelled` reads the cancel marks of the delivered messages) is not on this path: no mark is set before the test cancels, and the failed wait comes before the cancel.
+
+## Next
+
+- Reproduce under parallel stress (see the memory note `stub-backend-producer-race.md`).
+- Find if the chunk can stay in the buffer of the backend stream while the tool runs (the test comment says the backend yields the first chunk before the tool runs), so the wait can never be met in some orders.
+
+## Acceptance
+
+- [ ] The cause is found and written on this task.
+- [ ] A fix, or a test that waits on a real signal.
+- [ ] 0 failures of this test over 3 rounds of the stress. #test-flake
\ No newline at end of file

 assignees:
 - claude-code
+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m3f54t2w2rmc7da36rbca68a
+  text: |-
+    Research and reproduction at HEAD (fc01c7e).
+
+    Path of the first chunk: `HookedSessionBackend.streamResponse` yields `firstStreamedChunk` into an unbounded `AsyncThrowingStream`, then runs the tool hook. The default `streamResponseFragments` pulls from that stream through `ChunkIterator` (pull-based, no relay task). `streamGeneratingBody` yields each event to the stream of the reader. The consumer task of the test (a `Task {}` made on the main actor, so it runs on the main actor) appends the event to the `DeliveredEvents` actor. Nothing on this path waits for the tool, and nothing is cancelled before the test calls `cancel()`. So no order of tasks can hold the chunk back for ever. Only the scheduler can delay it.
+
+    Stress (swiftpm-testing-helper, 18 cores):
+    - Round A: 16 processes x 500 repetitions, filter on the one test. Load 5.0 to 5.3. 8000 runs, 0 chunk issues.
+    - Round B: 16 processes x 3 repetitions, whole bundle. Load 5.5 to 83.4. 48 runs of the test, 0 chunk issues. Other tests that use the 5-second `BoundedWait` bound failed at this load (for example HumanWaitGateTests "the second message waiting in the outbox", GenerationStallDiagnosticTests `SignalNeverArrived`).
+    - Round C: 12 processes x 4 repetitions of the whole bundle, and 8 processes x 60 repetitions of `AnswerCancellationTests`. Load 40.8 to 84.0. 528 runs of the test, 2 failures, both `BoundedWait.swift:114:25` "the first streamed chunk at the consumer was never observed inside the bound" (load1.log and load9.log, first repetition of the whole bundle, when all 1487 tests start at once). REPRODUCED.
+
+    Evidence of the cause: in both failed runs the only issue was the bounded wait. The later check `#expect(await delivered.events.contains(.textDelta(HookedSessionBackend.firstStreamedChunk)))`, which runs after `cancel()`, did not record an issue. So the chunk did reach the consumer, only after the 5-second wall-clock bound. If the chunk had stayed in the buffer of the backend stream, the cancel would have dropped it and that check would fail too. In that same run the test took 72.9 seconds for its repetitions.
+
+    Cause: the test time limit under load, not a delivery problem in production code. `BoundedWait.conditionReached` uses a wall-clock ceiling of 5 seconds; at load 80+ the main actor, which all @MainActor tests of the process share, and the consumer task get too few time slices to deliver the chunk inside it.
+
+    Decision: replace the bounded wait with an `AwaitedEvent` that the consumer task signals after it appends the first chunk. This is the real-signal wait of this suite (`AwaitedEvent.swift`, and `awaitCancelledUnwind`); only the `.timeLimit(.minutes(1))` of the suite ends it, as a ceiling on a fault. No production code changes.
+
+    Separate finding: load9.log (round C) ended with `_ContiguousArrayStorage deallocated with non-zero retain count 2` and no run summary. That is a crash of the process, not this test. See the new task I file for it if it is not ^vg6bmq6.
